payload.title: Representative inline-four four-stroke mechanism

model.title: Representative inline-four four-stroke mechanism
model.description: Unqualified teaching-model proposal for human review: four inline cylinders, crank-slider motion, half-speed camshafts, and synchronized illustrative stroke timing.
assumptions: Four cylinders numbered 1–4 along the crankshaft axis. Firing order is the illustrative conventional choice 1–3–4–2; cylinders 1/4 share crank phase, opposite cylinders 2/3.
Fixed illustrative crank radius is 0.04 m and connecting-rod length is 0.15 m. Cylinder spacing may be chosen later solely for teaching geometry, not as a measured specification.
Coordinates: cylinder axes point along +y, crankshaft axis along z, and crank-pin lateral displacement is x. Piston y is measured from the crankshaft axis.
elapsed_time defaults to 0 s, range 0–20 s. cam_cycle_rate defaults to 0.1 Hz, range 0.05–0.5 Hz. These are adjustable illustrative playback rates, not engine operating-speed predictions.

time_experiment: elapsed_time; step_seconds=0.02; playback_speed=1; reset_on_change=[cam_cycle_rate]; end_time_id=cycle_duration. Play advances one complete four-stroke cycle and stops; changing rate resets time atomically. Scrubbing elapsed_time inspects cycle position. Preserve pause, keyboard, mobile, reduced-motion and inspection controls.

The clock is capped mathematically at one cycle. Initial state is cylinder 1 at firing top dead centre, with zero elapsed playback time. This is prescribed kinematics, not a dynamic initial-value solution.
Cam angle uses a -pi reference offset. Crank rotation is twice that angle. Both camshafts use cam_angle and cam_cycle_rate; their illustrative drive has a fixed 2:1 crank-to-cam ratio.

Quarter flags are half-open cycle intervals, with the final endpoint assigned to quarter 3. Cylinder 1: expansion, exhaust, intake, compression. Cylinder 3: compression, expansion, exhaust, intake. Cylinder 4: intake, compression, expansion, exhaust. Cylinder 2: exhaust, intake, compression, expansion.

For each cylinder, intake-open and inward-flow cues use its intake quarter flag; exhaust-open and outward-flow cues use its exhaust quarter flag. Valves are instantaneously switched teaching states without overlap, lift profiles or actuator dynamics.

Spark events are qualitative boundary annotations at cycle fractions 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75 for cylinders 1, 3, 4 and 2 respectively. Quarter flags identify the ensuing expansion stroke, not spark duration.

The crank angle, crank-pin coordinates, piston positions and rod angles share the same phase. Opposite crank throws are obtained by a fixed pi rotation of the crank-pin geometry. Rod tilt is measured from +y toward -x.
Camshaft lobes, valves and passages are representative explanatory parts. Valve flags can bind simplified open/closed positions; flow cues indicate routing only, not a calculated gas velocity.
limitations: Combustion, spark ignition, gas exchange and conversion of chemical energy into mechanical work are explained qualitatively, not thermodynamically simulated.
No predictions of cylinder pressure, torque, power, fuel economy, emissions, heat transfer, friction, inertia, vibration or load response.
No diesel, two-stroke, variable-valve-timing or product-specific design claims. Timing excludes valve overlap and ignition advance.

No calibrated cam-lobe geometry, valve lift law, cam-drive belt/chain travel speed, gas-flow rate or spark-duration calculation. Use a representative rotating gear drive rather than an animated belt or chain.

Motion is prescribed by playback; the model does not calculate combustion-driven acceleration or explain starting dynamics. A complete engine cycle spans two crank revolutions and four piston strokes.
Boundary ignition annotations and component-role explanations are qualitative. They must not be presented as computed combustion events.

snapshot.unfinished_question: How does an inline four-cylinder car engine work?

definition.title: Inside an inline-four engine
definition.description: A simplified cutaway engine with four crank-slider assemblies and a representative geared camshaft drive.

parts.label: Cycle fraction
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Common timing state for all four cylinders; bounded 0–1.

parts.label: Crankshaft angle
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Continuous two-turn rotation, -2pi–2pi rad. Display scale 57.29577951308232, display unit degrees.

parts.label: Camshaft angle
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Both camshaft orientations, -pi–pi rad. Display scale 57.29577951308232, display unit degrees.

parts.label: Cylinder 1/4 piston-pin y
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Piston-pin position for cylinders 1 and 4; range 0.11–0.19 m. Fixed piston geometry follows this position.

parts.label: Cylinder 2/3 piston-pin y
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Piston-pin position for cylinders 2 and 3; range 0.11–0.19 m.

parts.label: Camshaft rotation rate
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Adjustable illustrative playback rate: default 0.1 Hz; range 0.05–0.5 Hz. One cam revolution per four-stroke cycle.

parts.label: Complete cycle duration
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Finite playback duration, independent of the clock; range 2–20 s.

limits: Illustrative construction, not measured engine geometry. All axes use 100 scene units per metre; cylinder spacing is an illustrative 0.10 m. The SI equations are unchanged.
Exactly 32 separately inspectable visible parts. Identical stationary sleeves, spark plugs and passage branches share inspection parts; each piston, rod and valve remains separately selectable.
Cylinders 1–4 lie along +Z at z=-15,-5,5,15. +Y is up; the crankshaft axis is Z. Crank radius is 0.04 m and rod pin spacing is 0.15 m.
Firing order is 1–3–4–2. Cylinders 1/4 share crank phase, opposite 2/3. A complete cycle spans two crank revolutions and four piston strokes.

Preserve cycle scrubbing, play/pause, adjustable illustrative playback rate, keyboard, mobile, reduced-motion and inspection controls. Playback stops at cycle_duration. Inactivity never resumes paused playback.

Cylinder 1 quarters: expansion, exhaust, intake, compression. Cylinder 3: compression, expansion, exhaust, intake. Cylinder 4: intake, compression, expansion, exhaust. Cylinder 2: exhaust, intake, compression, expansion.

Valve states and routing cues use the corresponding accepted quarter flags. Instantaneous switching has no overlap, calibrated lift law or actuator dynamics. Lobes illustrate timing, not computed cam contact.

Ignition is a qualitative boundary annotation at fractions 0,0.25,0.5,0.75 for cylinders 1,3,4,2. Expansion flags do not represent spark duration. Flow cues indicate direction, not calculated velocity or flow rate; no gas volume is modeled as a fixed-height solid beneath a moving piston boundary; gas routing remains qualitative rather than a solved flow field. No gas or oil circulation calculation

parts.label: Mounting base
parts.explanation: This sturdy base holds the teaching engine upright.

parts.label: Cylinder block
parts.explanation: The block holds the cylinders and supports the turning shafts. Open it to see the moving parts.

parts.label: Cylinder head and cam cover
parts.explanation: The head closes the cylinders and guides the valves. Its upper cover protects the camshafts.

parts.label: Oil sump
parts.explanation: This hollow bowl collects lubricating oil. Oil circulation is not shown.

parts.label: Crankshaft
parts.explanation: Offset pins connect the rods to this shaft. Piston travel and shaft rotation are linked through those pins.

parts.label: Five main bearing sleeves
parts.explanation: These hollow sleeves support the crankshaft while it turns.

parts.label: Four cylinder liners
parts.explanation: These hollow sleeves guide the pistons up and down.

parts.label: Piston 1
parts.explanation: Piston 1 slides inside its cylinder. Its crown is the top surface facing the burning mixture.

parts.label: Connecting rod 1
parts.explanation: This rod joins the piston pin to an offset crank pin. Its hollow ends allow the joints to turn.

parts.label: Piston 2
parts.explanation: Piston 2 moves with piston 3, but their strokes have different jobs.

parts.label: Connecting rod 2
parts.explanation: This rod links piston 2 to its crank pin. The joints let it lean as the crank turns.

parts.label: Piston 3
parts.explanation: Piston 3 moves with piston 2. Cylinder 3 has the second power stroke in this firing order.

parts.label: Connecting rod 3
parts.explanation: This rod links piston 3 to its crank pin.

parts.label: Piston 4
parts.explanation: Piston 4 follows piston 1, but their cycle stages are two strokes apart.

parts.label: Connecting rod 4
parts.explanation: This rod links piston 4 to its crank pin.

parts.label: Intake camshaft
parts.explanation: Raised lobes show how the intake valves are timed. This shaft turns once per complete engine cycle.

parts.label: Exhaust camshaft
parts.explanation: This shaft times the exhaust valves. It turns at half the crankshaft's rotation rate.

parts.label: Camshaft bearing sleeves
parts.explanation: These hollow sleeves keep both camshafts lined up while they turn.

parts.label: Crankshaft timing gear
parts.explanation: This small gear sends crankshaft rotation into the timing drive.

parts.label: Timing idler gear
parts.explanation: This middle gear carries rotation to both camshaft gears. Its fixed axle supports it while it turns.

parts.label: Intake timing gear
parts.explanation: This gear has twice as many teeth as the crankshaft gear. Two crank turns give one camshaft turn.

parts.label: Exhaust timing gear
parts.explanation: This gear keeps the exhaust camshaft turning at the same rate as the intake camshaft.

parts.label: Cylinder 1 intake valve
parts.explanation: This valve opens the entrance for fresh mixture. A valve is a movable seal.

parts.label: Cylinder 1 exhaust valve
parts.explanation: This valve opens the exit for burned gas.

parts.label: Cylinder 2 intake valve
parts.explanation: This valve admits fresh mixture during cylinder 2's intake stroke.

parts.label: Cylinder 2 exhaust valve
parts.explanation: This valve lets burned gas leave cylinder 2.

parts.label: Cylinder 3 intake valve
parts.explanation: This valve admits fresh mixture during cylinder 3's intake stroke.

parts.label: Cylinder 3 exhaust valve
parts.explanation: This valve lets burned gas leave cylinder 3.

parts.label: Cylinder 4 intake valve
parts.explanation: This valve admits fresh mixture during cylinder 4's intake stroke.

parts.label: Cylinder 4 exhaust valve
parts.explanation: This valve lets burned gas leave cylinder 4.

parts.label: Four spark plugs
parts.explanation: Each plug makes a spark that starts burning the compressed mixture. The spark marks here show timing, not a combustion calculation.

parts.label: Intake and exhaust passages
parts.explanation: These hollow paths carry fresh mixture in and burned gas out. Follow the two sides to their valves.

experiments.title: From piston to crankshaft
experiments.prompt: At the default 0.1 Hz rate, predict how piston 1 and its rod move when you scrub to 1.25 s. Compare with piston 2.
experiments.explanation: Piston 1 slides, its rod pivots, and the connected crankshaft turns. The piston-height readouts follow the declared crank-slider geometry; playback prescribes motion rather than calculating combustion forces.

experiments.title: Follow cylinder 1's valves
experiments.prompt: At 0.1 Hz, predict which cylinder 1 valve opens at 6.25 s. Scrub there, then inspect all four quarters.
experiments.explanation: Cylinder 1 follows expansion, exhaust, intake and compression. Its intake valve opens in the third quarter. Valve switching and routing cues are simplified teaching states; combustion and gas flow are not calculated.

experiments.title: Two crank turns, one cam turn
experiments.prompt: At 0.1 Hz, predict the crankshaft and camshaft rotation changes from 0 to 5 s. Inspect the timing gears and compare angle readouts.
experiments.explanation: The crankshaft gear drives the idler, which drives both camshaft gears. The crank angle changes twice as much as the cam angle. Matching piston heights need not mean matching strokes; expansion proceeds in order 1–3–4–2, with qualitative ignition boundary annotations.

experiments.title: Change the pace, not the mechanism
experiments.prompt: Predict how setting the camshaft playback rate to 0.2 Hz changes cycle duration. Then play and compare the same cycle stages.
experiments.explanation: Cycle duration is the reciprocal of camshaft rotation rate. Changing rate resets time atomically; the crank-to-cam ratio and prescribed geometry remain unchanged. This is illustrative playback speed, not a prediction of engine power or load response.

controls.help: Scrub the shared cycle phase; pistons, shafts and valve states hold after one complete cycle.
Set illustrative playback pace, not engine dynamics; changing it restarts time while preserving the 2:1 crank-to-cam ratio.

time_experiment.explanation: Start at cylinder 1 firing top dead centre. Cycle fraction is min(time × camshaft rate, 1); accepted crank-slider equations prescribe motion and quarter flags coordinate valves. Stop after one cycle: two crank turns and one cam turn. Rate changes restart time atomically. Preserve pause, reduced-motion, keyboard, mobile and inspection controls; inactivity never resumes playback.

coverage.explanation: Inspect component roles and connections in this simplified representative engine. Inspection separation is not physical operating motion. Combustion energy conversion is qualitative; no pressure, torque, power, economy, emissions or heat-transfer predictions are supported. Diesel, two-stroke, variable-valve-timing and product-specific designs are excluded.

Elapsed time sets the common phase, calculated piston positions and declared quarter-based valve states across four strokes. A stroke is one piston traversal, not a complete cycle. Combustion and directional routing cues remain qualitative; timing has no overlap or calibrated lift law.

Shared phase drives crank-slider motion and the fixed 2:1 crank-to-cam timing. Rate sets cycle duration. Compare cylinders using the declared 1–3–4–2 expansion sequence; ignition markers explain boundary timing qualitatively, not computed spark duration, torque or combustion-driven acceleration.

outcomes: Identify the cylinders, pistons, connecting rods, crankshaft, camshafts, valves, spark plugs, and intake and exhaust passages, and explain their roles.
Follow intake, compression, combustion and expansion, and exhaust through a complete four-stroke cycle.
Explain how piston motion turns the crankshaft and how valve timing and ignition coordinate the four cylinders to deliver successive power strokes.

generation_quality.scope: Recipe, label, connection and dependency checks only. Dependency paths do not prove numeric change. Overlap, recognizability, physical correctness and child usability require separate evaluation.

visual.scope: Eight fitted views; projected bounds, center-ray occlusion, conservative bounding-box overlaps and estimated two-line label capacity. These heuristics do not replace rendered-image or child usability review.

sampled_quality.scope: Defaults, five points per input plus presets, a midpoint context for apparently inactive controls, all-input endpoints, and lesson experiments. Finite geometry and observed changes only; no proof of scientific accuracy, recognizability or complete state-space coverage.
